batchIdentityNotes.assessment: 1530 to 1650 southeastern outline; broad homeland approximation. Shared narrative explicitly distinguishes Mississippi Band and Oklahoma Choctaw Nation, with removal and separate constitutional histories.
1492 to 1500 southeastern homeland outline. Same Choctaw people, not a separate extinct polity. Shares card with historical mainland record and later Oklahoma phase, all dates treated as coverage.

MAJOR ANACHRONISM:1492 to 1500 polygon is in southeastern Oklahoma, a homeland associated with nineteenth-century removal. Public opening and ending explicitly warn. Source narrative covers1830s removal and1834 Indian Territory constitution; no geometry repair performed.
1530 to 1650 southeastern outline. Shared narrative covers homeland, removal and continuing government, distinguishing Chickasaw identity from Choctaw.
1492 to 1500 southeastern Chickasaw homeland outline. Same nation as chickasaw, defensible broader-phase association.

MAJOR ANACHRONISM:1492 to 1500 polygon is south-central Oklahoma, associated with nineteenth-century removal and1855 separation. Public opening and ending warn; shared card explicitly covers these phases. No geometry repair performed.
1530 to 1783 central Plains outline; four bands and Kitkahahki-specific village evidence distinguished. Broader continuing-nation narrative explicitly covers later removal.
1492 to 1500 central Plains approximation, same Pawnee nation context. Not a separate polity; no precise foundation inferred.

MAJOR ANACHRONISM:1492 to 1500 Oklahoma polygons (including a tiny second feature) are associated with1874 to 1875 migration and later allotment. Public opening and ending warn; no geometry repair performed.

1492 to 1715 very broad outline across western/central Canada. Cultural and linguistic umbrella, not unified empire; Plains, eastern and other community evidence identified in passages. No extinction at1715.
1530 to 1783 northern Plains outline; alliance/nations distinguished. Shared with Niitsitapi cultural homeland record without equating the confederacy with one centralized state.

1492 to 1500 very broad northern Plains cultural outline. Same Blackfoot/Niitsitapi context; periods include buffalo life, later treaties and present communities. Geography not a fixed legal boundary.

MAJOR INCOMPLETE OUTLINE:1492 to 1500 bounds53.28 to 55.86N omit southern Haida Gwaii and extend toward southeastern Alaska. Public opening warns; SGang Gwaay example explicitly south of outline. Narrative follows island/community identity, not polygon accuracy.
1492 to 1500 broad southeast Alaska/coastal outline. No single Tlingit kingdom inferred. Kiks.adi and Huna examples identified locally;1804 resistance and modern institutions extend beyond coverage.

1492 to 1500 outline broadly spans Mohawk Valley to St. Lawrence. Mohawk-specific card, not alias of general Haudenosaunee. Distinct Kahnawake/Akwesasne/Grand River histories and governments; no national extinction at1500.
